title: Geo-partitioned throughput SLAs with progressive evacuation choreography
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and implement a region-aware throughput SLA layer and an associated progressive evacuation choreography for multi-zone dedicated fleets. The feature must allow customers to declare geo-partitioned throughput commitments (e.g., 500 RPS in eu-west and 200 RPS in us-east) with rules for staged failover that respect data residency and minimize wide-area traffic spikes. This ticket covers control-plane schema, runtime routing primitives, drain choreography, and a minimal console surface for SLA and evacuation visibility.
background_and_motivation: Customers using Dedicated capacity want contractual throughput guarantees per region for compliance and performance. Current placement is coarse-grained and drains cause blunt full-fleet failovers that violate residency constraints or cause sudden cost/latency regressions. We need a choreography that gradually shifts load, honors per-region residency locks, and exposes predictable behavior under pressure (node loss, zone outage, or capacity exhaustion).
goals: Support per-region throughput commitments and overprovision thresholds
Provide staged evacuation (progressive spillover) with configurable windows and backoff
Enforce data residency: requests tagged with residency must not be routed outside allowed geographies unless explicitly authorized
Expose SLA health, projected bleed-over, and expected latency/cost impact in Console/alerts
Minimize cold-start cost by integrating prewarm hooks into evacuation windows
non_goals: Full commercial billing integration (will be separate billing ticket)
Rich multitenant quota marketplace — MVP supports explicit per-customer region commitments only
Complex predictive placement algorithms beyond simple heuristics (future work)
acceptance_criteria: API: customers can create or update geo throughput commitments via Redwood API and Console
Runtime: when a zone becomes degraded, the system performs a progressive evacuation in configured steps rather than a full immediate failover
Residency: requests with residency tags are not routed outside permitted regions unless 'residency_override' is explicitly set on the commitment and flagged (audited)
Observability: Console shows per-region committed vs actual throughput, evacuation progress with timestamps, and cost delta estimate
Failure modes: documented rollback and automated fallback that limits latency degradation to < 50ms p95 delta for staged sizes in lab tests
high_level_design: Introduce a GeoSLA object in the control plane that maps customer -> region -> min_throughput and optional residency policy. The Orchestrator will subscribe to GeoSLA delta events and convert them to: (1) placement hints to the slot allocator, (2) a staged evacuation plan when capacity falls below thresholds, and (3) routing policy updates (route weights and soft prefills). Evacuation choreography runs as a state machine: GracefulDrain -> Prefix-KV-Flush -> Prewarm-Bump -> Weighted-Spill -> Final-Evacuate. Each step has tunable windows and health checks. The runtime will expose hooks to drain in-memory KV caches and allow short-lived cross-region KV proxying under explicit residency_override and audit logging.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: We evaluated two approaches: an optimistic instant failover that switches routes immediately (simple, lower implementation cost) vs. a progressive choreography (complex, better UX and cost outcomes). We chose progressive choreography because customers with residency constraints prefer predictable, auditable transitions even at implementation complexity cost. We considered a fully centralized global allocator but rejected it for latency and single-point-of-failure concerns; instead a distributed orchestrator with consistent control-plane events will be used.
schema_changes: Add GeoSLA table with fields: customer_id, region_code, min_throughput_rps, max_burst_rps, residency_policy (ENUM: none, restrict, allow-with-audit), residency_override_allowed (boolean string), evacuation_windows (JSON stringified config). Control plane will version GeoSLA objects; runtime subscribes to updates through the existing event bus.
runtime_changes: Orchestrator: implement evacuation state machine and health-check hooks. Router: support weighted spill and per-request residency tags. Serving runtime: graceful KV drain API and prewarm endpoint. Slot allocator: honor placement hints when allocating new slots to respect region commitments.
console_changes: Add 'Geo Throughput' panel under Dedicated -> Fleets. Show committed vs actual throughput, evacuation timeline, and a small action surface to start a manual evacuation or set an emergency residency_override. Add alerts for when actual < 90% of committed for > 5 minutes.
implementation_plan: Control-plane: GeoSLA schema and CRUD API (2w)
Orchestrator: evacuation state machine + subscription handlers (3w)
Router: residency-tag propagation and weighted spill implementation (2w)
Serving runtime: KV drain and prewarm hooks (2w)
Console: panels and manual controls + alerting (1w)
Gradual rollout behind feature flag and invite-only customers (1w)

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Evacuation windows too long — customers may observe degraded throughput for longer than acceptable. Mitigation: expose aggressive and conservative presets, allow customers to opt into fast-failover for non-residency traffic.
Risk: Cross-region KV proxying violates compliance. Mitigation: default to deny; enable only when residency_override_allowed is set and log to immutable audit stream. Require opt-in and SRE review.
Risk: Complexity in orchestrator introduces bugs. Mitigation: small incremental rollout, feature flags, and Chaos monkeying in staging prior to any GA customers.
Risk: Cost of prewarm increases unit economics. Mitigation: prewarm sizing heuristics based on recent request velocity and short prewarm TTLs; estimate cost impact shown in Console before enabling.
test_plan: Unit tests for GeoSLA CRUD and validation rules
Integration tests for evacuation state transitions with simulated zone loss
Load tests verifying committed throughput honored under variable cluster sizes
Compliance tests ensuring residency-tagged requests never exit region unless override is enabled
Chaos test: terminate 1 zone and validate progressive spill keeps p95 latency delta within target
rollout_plan: Feature-flag deployment (control-plane + orchestrator + router) to staging
Invite-only early customers with noncritical workloads
Collect metrics for 2 weeks, tune default evacuation windows
Open to more customers behind an enrollment flow in Console
GA after two successful customer pilots and SRE sign-off
open_questions: What defaults should we set for eviction windows for small vs large fleets?
Should residency_override require legal acceptance (e.g., signed waiver) for enterprise customers?
Is there appetite to allow soft residency (best-effort) for certain customers to trade cost for availability?
notes: This ticket is intentionally focused on deterministic choreography and auditability. Future follow-ups will explore predictive prewarming and dynamic contractual pricing tied to SLA enforcement.
